notes.title: An Ode to Restraint: Lessons from the Tim Cook Legacy
notes.text: Market cap rose from $1.68 billion at the start of Jobs's tenure to over $4 trillion at end-2025; Cook added $3.64 trillion. Jobs-era price appreciation 47.19% a year compounded (1997-2011). Revenue grew 23.67% a year under Jobs and 8.52% (2012-2025) under Cook, with nearly $800 billion of buybacks, dividends since 2012 and a $17 billion debt issue in 2013; net debt always negative. Its share of Mag Seven capex fell from 8.04% to 3.02%. He calls it a mature, cash-returning, cautious business and says he has been a shareholder through much of both tenures.
